description.narrative:
With the legal challenges faced by KADUAMI, specifically against the two(2) officers and a partner representative, related to alleged violations of the Terrorism Financing Suppression and Prevention Act, and with the possibility of their accounts to be frozen, KADUAMI, through its Executive Director Ms. Leonida, has expressed if Voice could transfer the final tranche to a different organization, and hence this project accommodating this request by transferring the final tranche to another Voice grantee-partner CYC.
AboutKADUAMI's project implemented with the support of Voice: Full Project Title: Building a Web of Safety and Care for Women Human Rights Defenders
The change that this project wishes to contribute is that the RHGs regained their confidence to continue perform theirroles in their respective works. The constantthreats they experienced are significantly reduced. The change is basically at the level of the individuals that has an impact at the organizational and social level. At the individual level, the RHG are indicating increase in confidence because of established web of support. The red-tagging and vilification against the RGHs that proliferated during the pandemic period and had worsened overtime would decrease when they are given the opportunity to countermeasures with their access to legal support. The RHGs experienced red-tagging through makeshift posters, leafleting, tarpaulins, painting on public infrastructure (i.e.waiting sheds, walls, etc.) and posting malicious information online proliferated during the pandemic. A woman leader from Isabela accounted that her name appeared seven hundred (700) times in different posters in different areas. Another leader from Isabela was also visited by military agents twenty-five (25) times at her home. A leader from Cagayan also reported that she was interrogatedfor a whole month by military agents who camped near their house. She narrated that they talked to her from morning to afternoon even when she was doing household chores. Familymembers are witnesses to the abuses. In La Union province, the daughter of aPOleader broke down in tears when military kept on visiting their home and continuously interrogating his mother. In Cagayan province, the son of a woman leader had a heated argument and confrontation with a military officer for repeatedly harassing hismother. In Ilocos Norte, the son of a peasant leader was interrogated in his own school. The military officers kept on asking the whereabouts ofhis mother and father who had beenin sanctuary. In the same province, a daughter was with her friends attendinga church activity when military officers cornered her, andshe was asked to answer questions. This prompted the girl not to attend church activities in the meantime. In all theseincidents, human rights defenders need to be safe and protected in doingtheirwork. Human rights defense is essential in achieving food security and human development. It is in this context that KADUAMI’s effort will focus on this. Within the organization, KADUAMI improved its human rights work by creating a web of support that caters to victims of human rights violations in its scope of work in Northern Luzon. With established linkages to professional service providers and a community support system, the rightsholders group can address mental health concerns and can refer membersof the community that need professional intervention. They can acquire knowledge and skills from trainings that provides livelihood opportunities for RHGs that lost the source of income. RHGs who are facing judicial harassment can seek legal representation from lawyers. A community support system is in place initiated by family members and advocates of the RHGs and are active in campaign and advocacy.

participating-org.narrative:
Cordilleran Youth Center Inc. Who are we: # A non-profit, non-stock, non-government organization that is committed to help arouse, organize and mobilize the youth and students in advancing the interests and welfare of the indigenous peoples of the Cordillera. # CYC provides services to various indigenous and non-indigenous youth and students# organizations. It also coordinates various activities spearheaded by CYC partner organizations.
What are our programs: # Education, training, animation and tutorial Preparation, dissemination and discussion of popular education materials on IP rights, youth and students rights and other issues. # Organizing and networking Helps in the formation and consolidation of community-base and school-based organizations. Develops and strengthen links and cooperation among youth in the countr and abroad. # Campaigns and advocacy Launches and participates in systematic and sustainedactivities towards the recognition of rights of indigenous peoples and that of the youth and students in particular. # Culture, heritage and development Launches and encourages youth participation in activities that seeks to strengthen, and develop indigenous social, cultural institutions and practices and enhance the cross-cultural learning. # Socio-economic and disaster risk reduction and management This is implemented through education and mobilizing the indigenous youth to uphold their role as protectors of their resources and communities
